<reason>A wins by defending the proposition’s explicit privacy constraint while explaining how provider checks add protection where household controls are absent. B raises legitimate implementation and displacement concerns, but repeatedly substitutes existing intrusive systems for the proposed constrained mandate and asserts deployment limitations too categorically. A directly answers both pressure questions and acknowledges displacement; B never adequately supports its crucial claim that children lacking parental controls will simply evade provider checks.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s closing exposes B’s decisive leap: an inactive caregiver does not imply a determined circumventer. This preserves A’s coverage advantage and shows why displacement alone cannot establish that mandatory checks produce net harm.</best_rebuttal>
